title: Molten Chloride Small Modular Reactor Performance Characteristics for Data Center Operation
problem: Data centers require high-reliability power; conventional large nuclear reactors have large footprint. Molten chloride small modular reactors (SMRs) promising but behavior under data center load profiles (mismatched power rating, sub-maximum capacity) unexplored.
motivation: Molten chloride fast reactors marketed for data center power but lack characterization of operational dynamics at partial load. Understanding steady-state behavior below maximum capacity critical for deployment feasibility.
method: They simulated a molten chloride small modular reactor using MOOSE (a software tool for modeling how heat, fluid flow, and materials behave together in complex systems). The reactor ran at partial capacity with control rods held at 60% open, and they analyzed the steady thermal and fluid-flow behavior—how heat and coolant flow stabilize—under these below-maximum-power conditions.
key_novelty: First simulation of how a molten chloride small modular reactor behaves when running below full capacity, as it would need to in real data center operation.
contributions: Characterization of steady-state behavior with control rods at 60% open
Data center power delivery feasibility insights
limitations: No performance metrics reported (abstract describes simulation approach only)
Comparison with other SMR designs absent
Data center load profile characteristics not discussed
Economic and practical deployment analysis absent
primary_theme: Molten chloride SMR simulation for data center power
